$comment: Sanitization gate config for agentic-startup-generalist. The deterministic layer (secrets/PII) needs no tuning; the semantic layer is taught what 'a particular' means for this domain below.
$comment_prefixes: Paths whose CONTENT could leak operator/venture particulars. Top-level *.md (README, CONTRIBUTING) are always included automatically.

semantic.$comment_domain_noun: A 'particular' belongs to one venture — one startup this agent serves. The package is the generic substrate; a venture's board, metrics, team, and roadmap are its particulars and must never land here.
flag_examples: personal names of founders, team members, advisors, investors, or customers tied to a specific venture
specific company or product names tied to one active venture (not generic/public reference)
revenue, ARR, burn, runway, valuation, cap-table, or pricing figures for a specific venture
retention, activation, conversion, or cohort metrics from a specific venture's real data
Notion database/page IDs, Slack channel or workspace IDs, Slack user IDs, Linear/Jira project keys, or GitHub org/repo names tied to one venture
a messaging or account identifier tied to a real person — a Signal/Telegram UUID, a contact phone, an allowlisted user ID (these belong in deployment config/secrets, never in the package)
internal hostnames, tailnet addresses, IPs, or deployment targets for a venture's infrastructure
a codename or label that identifies one particular venture (e.g. used as a skill name or heading)
security findings, vulnerabilities, or audit results tied to a specific venture's systems
dates, locations, or deal details that only make sense for one venture
do_not_flag_examples: generic methodology ("how to structure a weekly rollup", "how to grade a PMF signal", "how to frame a decision for a human gate")
tool, API, library, or product names used generically (Notion, Slack, Linear, GitHub, PostHog, semgrep)
well-known public reference material or frameworks used illustratively
generic role nouns (founder, operator, maintainer) not attached to a named person

this package's OWN identity: the maintaining org (NimbleCo, NimbleCoOrg) and this repository's own name (agentic-startup-generalist). The package is published BY that org — its own name is not a venture particular. A DIFFERENT venture's org or repo still flags.
this package's own MIT copyright line, and the canonical clone/install URL of this repository
the runtime this package targets by design (hermes-agent-mt, Swarm Map) — a documented dependency, not a leaked particular

deterministic.$comment: The credential/PII layer runs with NO external dependencies and FAILS CLOSED. These patterns are conservative defaults; add your own. Allowlist false-positives by exact line substring in 'allow_substrings'.
deterministic.$comment_skip_paths: DO NOT REMOVE. Path prefixes the deterministic layer does NOT scan. tests/ legitimately holds credential-SHAPED fixtures (sk-ant-..., AKIA...) to exercise the detectors; scanning them self-flags and hard-fails a clean repo. The scanner defaults this key to EMPTY when absent, so omitting it is not a no-op — it breaks the gate. The upstream usecase-package-template's SETUP.md section-2 example omits this key; that is a bug in that template, not guidance. Keep this tight — only paths that intentionally hold pattern-shaped non-secrets.
